newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cen.bank raises one-week rate to 85 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania cen.bank raises one-week rate to 85 pct.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) on Thursday lifted the minimum permitted rate for its one-week refinancing funds by 5.0 percentage points, to 85 percent, continuing to tighten its monetary policies.
The BNR said it had slightly increased the refinancing funds on offer to 600 billion lei ($97.6 million) from last week's 550 billion.
The central bank's move aims to temper soaring inflation, restrain expansion of the money supply and drain liquidity from the money market in a bid to prop up the local leu currency.

The leu has fallen some 50 percent to 6,150/200 to the dollar since January 1. Year-on-year inflation rose to 56.9 percent last December, nearly triple the 20 percent target agreed with the International Monetary Fund for 1996.
Interbank rates, now trading at around 80 percent for short-term funds, are expected to rise following the BNR's move against the background of a cash-starved money market.

Romania's new centrist coalition is currently holding talks with IMF for fresh credits. Last year, the Fund suspended loans to Romania in response to foreign exchange market curbs and overspending by the former leftist government.
